subject.title: Feature: inbound 'reply in thread' / 'rit' user directive

question: Should OpenClaw make natural-language suffixes like `reply in thread` or `rit` a built-in cross-channel reply override, and if so which trigger words and `replyToMode` override semantics are acceptable by default?
rationale: This is not a broken existing contract; broad suffixes can silently alter user intent, optional config would add schema surface, and forcing replies could override current per-channel reply policy.

options.title: Specify a narrow core directive
options.body: Approve a small default-on suffix contract, likely excluding ambiguous bare `thread`, and require implementation to strip every agent-visible body field with tests for supported threaded channels.

options.title: Keep it prompt or plugin owned
options.body: Leave natural-language phrasing to prompts or plugins and keep core limited to explicit reply tags and configured reply modes.

options.title: Require explicit config first
options.body: Allow this only behind a documented config key with schema, docs, and tests, accepting the extra config surface intentionally.

recommendation.title: Specify a narrow core directive
recommendation.body: Approve a small default-on suffix contract, likely excluding ambiguous bare `thread`, and require implementation to strip every agent-visible body field with tests for supported threaded channels.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest history signal on the central inbound finalizer and reply-threading policy files.
